open_obligations: Check that Khan et al. (2024) use QuALITY and a fixed-round, non-recursive debate protocol
Note that the remark is collective; confirm nothing in the passage singles out Khan et al.
out.other_title: Debate helps non-expert LLM and human judges on QuALITY; persuasive debaters help more
out.rationale: The authors characterise prior empirical work, including Khan et al., as limited in dataset and protocol depth, which shows a limit of the scope of such results without new data and without arguing that Khan et al.'s method is flawed. The remark is made collectively about five studies, so it applies to Khan et al. only as one member of that group.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: Whether existing empirical debate results support the safety case's claims; holds as a limit of scope (dataset, recursion depth), not of the reported accuracy gains

text: The authors cite Khan et al. (2024) among the studies of debate's practical effectiveness and say there is only limited data: most previous experiments use the QuALITY dataset and simple debate protocols with low recursive depth. They list key questions such as whether training reliably reaches equilibrium and whether obfuscated arguments actually emerge as predicted.
title: Buhl et al. cite Khan et al. among limited data on debate's practical effectiveness
